title: Sample mean
context: The starting point of any analysis.
task: Set result to the mean of the sample column x, rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Sample median
task: Set result to the median of sample x, rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Most common group
task: Set result to the most frequent group in measurements (a string).

title: Range of the sample
task: Set result to the range (max − min) of sample x, rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Sample variance
task: Set result to the sample variance of x (ddof=1), rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Sample standard deviation
task: Set result to the sample standard deviation of x (ddof=1), rounded to 2 decimals.

title: First quartile
task: Set result to the 25th percentile (Q1) of sample x, rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Interquartile range
task: Set result to the IQR of sample x, rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Count of observations
task: Set result to the number of rows in sample (an int).

title: Total value
task: Set result to the sum of the value column in measurements, rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Mean per group
task: Set result to a Series of mean value per group (A, B), rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by group.

title: Std per group
task: Set result to a Series of std (ddof=1) of value per group, rounded to 2 decimals, sorted by group.

title: Group sizes
task: Set result to a Series of counts per group, sorted by group.

title: Even die roll
task: Set result to the probability of rolling an even number on a fair six-sided die, as a fraction rounded to 4 decimals.

title: Conversion rate
task: Set result to the control conversion rate = control conversions / visitors, rounded to 4 decimals.

title: Treatment conversion rate
task: Set result to the treatment conversion rate, rounded to 4 decimals.

title: Standard normal CDF
task: Set result to the standard-normal CDF at 1.96, rounded to 4 decimals, using scipy stats.

title: Normal quantile
task: Set result to the z-value where the standard-normal CDF equals 0.975, rounded to 4 decimals.

title: Binomial probability
task: Set result to P(X = 3) for X ~ Binomial(n=10, p=0.5), rounded to 4 decimals.

title: Poisson probability
task: Set result to P(X = 2) for X ~ Poisson(mu=3), rounded to 4 decimals.

title: Standardise one value
context: How many SDs from the mean is x = 190?
task: Set result to the z-score of 190 using the sample x mean and std (ddof=1), rounded to 3 decimals.

title: Count of outliers
task: Set result to the number of sample x values with an absolute z-score above 2 (population std, ddof=0) (an int).
answer:
x = sample['x'].to_numpy()
z = (x - x.mean()) / x.std()
result = int((np.abs(z) > 2).sum())

title: Hours vs score correlation
context: Do more study hours track higher scores?
task: Set result to the Pearson correlation between hours and score in regression, rounded to 3 decimals.

title: Skewness
task: Set result to the skewness of sample x, rounded to 3 decimals, using scipy stats.

title: Standard error of the mean
task: Set result to the standard error of the mean of sample x (ddof=1), rounded to 3 decimals.

title: Difference in group means
task: Set result to mean(B) − mean(A) from measurements, rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Mean improvement
task: Set result to the mean of (after − before) across paired subjects, rounded to 2 decimals.

title: 90th percentile
task: Set result to the 90th percentile of sample x, rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Coefficient of variation
task: Set result to the coefficient of variation of sample x (std ddof=1 / mean), rounded to 4 decimals.

title: Normal probability in a range
task: Set result to that probability, rounded to 4 decimals, using scipy.

title: Complement
task: Set result to the probability of at least one head in 3 fair coin flips, rounded to 4 decimals.

title: Five-number summary min
task: Set result to the minimum of sample x, rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Mean score
task: Set result to the mean score in regression, rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Max value in group B
task: Set result to the maximum value among group B rows in measurements, rounded to 2 decimals.
